design_decision.ownership: Generic, content-agnostic obstacle-placement mechanism (ObstacleSpec, DungeonRegionParams.Obstacles, placeRegionObstacles) lives in encounter/dungeon.go alongside InitDungeon -- it never references crypt/coffin/altar/etc, mirroring the file's existing Theme-is-opaque discipline. Crypt-specific content (the 5 approved Ref strings + which specs go in entrance/corridor/boss + the concrete CryptDungeonParams constructor) lives in a NEW file, encounter/crypt_dungeon.go, in the SAME module -- justified because ADR-0034 already classifies the `encounter` module as the (migration-pending) dnd5e rulebook loop, encounter/go.mod already depends on rulebooks/dnd5e by pseudo-version, and the repo's own test fixtures (dungeon_test.go's threeRegionDungeonParams / dungeonThemeCrypt) already treat 'the first crypt template's shape as encounter-owned content. Adding a NEW cross-module dependency from rulebooks/dnd5e -> encounter (which does not exist today) to host this instead would require publishing+tagging encounter and bumping rulebooks/dnd5e's go.mod for zero architectural benefit, since encounter already has the coupling in the other direction and no host (rpg-api) wiring exists yet either way (out of scope per #692).
design_decision.reserved_row_invariant: Placement candidates for EVERY region exclude the full doorRow row (all local x in [0,width)), not just the pre-existing required-path segment -- this single, simple, generic rule provably satisfies both 'required path stays clear' (a subset of the row) and the boss archetype's 'primary playable axis (>6 hex steps) stays clear' (the row spans the region's FULL width, always > the size-invariant floor validateDungeonParams already enforces at construction time).
